column1: # Publishability gates for every step: preregister estimands; prove enough data with power/precision,
# minimum independent sources and rows per declared slice, time/source diversity, and held-out reserve;
# execute a genuine LoRA/QLoRA weight-update arm on a pinned base and retain config, logs, resources,
# adapter hash, and before/after predictions. Prompt-only Modelfiles are controls, not fine-tuning.
# Missing training dependencies are a failed arm and keep the Architectural Drift Report non-publishable.

column3: Reproduce and critically audit tiny-fleet/docs/tiny-fleet-drift-report.md as a candidate Architectural Drift Report methodology: inspect snapshot selection, corpus extraction, Modelfiles/prompts, embedding implementation, model-capacity comparison, and every reported number; separate true fine-tuning from prompt conditioning and record missing provenance or unsupported claims.

Improve the Architectural Drift Report into a general, publishable, usable protocol: repository/snapshot selection, license-safe corpus construction, temporal and file-level leakage controls, frozen prompts, structural baselines, generative tests, embedding/calibration metrics, uncertainty, and minimum artifact/run manifest; choose at least two materially different public or local repos for a pilot.

Implement and test a reproducible dependency-light evaluator in tiny-fleet (or a clearly justified companion tool) that can run the improved drift experiment across repos and snapshots, with provenance-rich manifests, deterministic structural metrics, model/capacity controls, negative controls, and an explicit adapter for genuine LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning when torch/transformers/peft are available.

Run and verify the evaluator on the selected repos and multiple snapshot intervals, comparing prompt-only Modelfile conditioning against actual fine-tuning where dependencies permit and recording blocked arms honestly; publish raw manifests, outputs, scores, similarity/confidence intervals, sensitivity analyses, and a usability/reproducibility report.

Independently inspect or rerun the improved Architectural Drift Report study, verify that artifacts are fresh, provenance-linked, reproducible, and publishable, test leakage and negative controls, and assess whether each reported score measures vocabulary drift, conceptual drift, architectural drift, or an uncalibrated mixture; publish concrete pass/fail findings and required corrections.

Integrate the verified methodology into tiny-fleet documentation and tooling: define the canonical publishable report schema, limitations and interpretation rules, reusable commands, weekly/time-series extension, repo onboarding checklist, result usability criteria, and a prioritized roadmap for full small-model fine-tuning experiments; do not claim generality beyond the repos and arms actually measured.

Review the complete improved Architectural Drift Report methodology against the request, confirm every claimed capability has a real tested and independently verified artifact, and close with links to the reproducible protocol, cross-repo results, validator tests, usability evidence, and any explicit unresolved dependency or evidence gap.
